sections.sectionSummaryBrief: There is an additional advantage in the Priestly Blessing, as its flow comes from above the chain of descent, combining both a transcendent source and the mode of a command.

translations.translation: And there is an additional advantage in the Priestly Blessing,
that the flow of the Priestly Blessing is from above the chain of descent.
For blessing in general is to draw down what already exists in the source and not something new,
for in this matter prayer has an advantage over blessing,
that through prayer a new will is created.
And in the Priestly Blessing there are both advantages,
that the flow is from above the chain of descent,
and in the manner of a command.
And likewise is it regarding the flow that comes through Torah,
which has both advantages,
that the flow is from above the chain of descent and in the manner of a command.
And this is the advantage of the flow that comes through Torah
(of many)
over the flow that comes through prayer
(of many),
that the flow through Torah is in a manner that he is the master of the flow.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Even though the Priestly Blessing is a separate commandment, the Sages established it within prayer, showing that through prayer one reaches the transcendent flow of the Priestly Blessing, and similarly Torah study draws the higher flow of prayer.

translations.translation: A)
And behold, even though the Priestly Blessing is a commandment in its own right,
the Sages established it within prayer.
And from this it is understood,
that although prayer is from below to above, nevertheless through prayer one reaches the flow of the Priestly Blessing, which is from above to below.
And based on this, one may add in the lesson of the a fortiori argument,
that just as prayer and the Priestly Blessing,
although they are different matters,
for prayer is a request
(from below to above)
and the Priestly Blessing is a command
(from above to below),
and nevertheless through prayer one reaches the Priestly Blessing,
so too is it regarding Torah and prayer,
that although the flow of the revelation of the light of Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent, which comes through the study of Torah
(in its own right)
is lower than the flow of the revelation of the light of Ein Sof that comes through prayer
(as above in section 8),
nevertheless,
through the study of Torah there is drawn
(afterward)
also the flow that comes through prayer, which is above the flow of the revelation of the light of Ein Sof of Torah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This lesson itself is an a fortiori argument: since prayer from below reaches the Priestly Blessing from above, certainly Torah study, which is itself a transcendent flow, draws the even higher flow of prayer, because the person becomes master over it.

translations.translation: And one may add,
that this lesson itself is in the manner of an a fortiori argument.
For prayer is from below to above and the Priestly Blessing is from above to below,
and nevertheless through prayer one reaches the Priestly Blessing,
so regarding Torah and prayer,
that even the flow of Torah
(in its own right)
is a revelation of the light of Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent, only that this flow is lower than the flow of prayer,
that through Torah there is drawn also the flow of prayer,
is all the more so and an a fortiori argument.
And it may be said,
that through the fact that Torah is the Torah of the person who engages in Torah, who is the master, as it were, over the Torah,
through this he becomes master also over the level of the flow of prayer that is drawn into Torah.
And this is that the lesson of Torah and prayer is in the measure of a fortiori,
for the flow in prayer that comes through Torah has an advantage over the flow of prayer in its own right.
